deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a page of German prose notes on ancient Greek history, apparently lecture or school notes. It continues the narrative of Philip II of Macedon from the previous page and leads into the next.

Content, in order:
(1) In '357' Philip takes Amphipolis. He promises Potidaea to the Olynthians and deceives the Athenians with other promises.
(2) He seizes Mount Pangaeus and draws 1,000,000 (Thaler, abbreviated) a year from its gold mines.
(3) His next undertaking concerns Thessaly. The notes say the Aleuadae ruled Pherae and oppressed other Thessalian cities, which in '358' turned to Philip. He defeats the Aleuadae, makes Thessaly a province and concludes an alliance with the Thessalians.
(4) The following year the Sacred War ('h. Krieg' = heiliger Krieg) gives him a second occasion to enter Thessaly.
(5) He tries to enter Greece proper, but the Athenians hold the pass of Thermopylae. He withdraws and besieges Olynthus ('358'). The Athenians send a fleet and an army, but treachery had already delivered the city to him; this sentence continues on the next page.

No derivation, formula or computation appears; the only number besides dates is a revenue figure. The hand and the content look like a student's history notebook rather than mathematical work by Gauss, so it serves no mathematical problem.
errors: Historical, not mathematical. The Aleuadae were the ruling family of Larissa, not the rulers of Pherae. The oppressors were the tyrants of Pherae (Lycophron and others), and it was the Aleuadae who appealed to Philip. The notes reverse this, including 'Er besiegte die Aleuaden'.

Dates are inconsistent or anachronistic. The Thessalian intervention and the Athenian block at Thermopylae belong to 353/352 BC, not 358. The siege of Olynthus was 349-348 BC, not 358. On the next page, peace with Athens (Peace of Philocrates) was 346, not 357.
The Pangaeus revenue is usually given as about 1000 talents a year. The figure of 1,000,000 Thaler is a period conversion, not an ancient figure.
deep.surprise_reason: The page is a narrative of Greek history (Philip II of Macedon) with no mathematical content. It is probably not even Gauss's own work, but a student's notebook bound into the bundle.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 likely reads 'und den Athenern spiegelte er was anderes vor' (or 'das und anderes'). The image shows 'und andres vor' on line 3.
'Pang{ä}us': the blue insertion is a 'g' (Pan[g]äus), i.e. Mount Pangaeus.
The end of line 5 is an abbreviation for Thaler after '1000000'.
Line 6, 'Jetzt ging sein erster Versuch auf Thessalien': the preposition is uncertain, possibly 'an' or 'von'.
'ein Sieges{b}ündniß' is doubtful. The blue insertion appears to correct the word to '...bündniß', most likely just '(Schutz-)Bündniß'.
The dates '358' in lines 8 and 14 are as written in the manuscript, though historically wrong.
